# caption_verifier

**In one sentence:** The CaptionVerifierStep: renders each caption back into a picture with a text-to-image model, so you can see what the caption really "says" to a model and mark it correct, generic or wrong (and edit it).

## Why it exists
A caption can read fine to a person yet make an image model draw something else. Rendering the caption is a quick test of how a text encoder (the part of an image model that turns words into numbers) understands it. Bad captions are flagged so the caption step re-captions them on its next run.

## What's inside
| File / folder | What it does |
|---|---|
| `step.py` | `run()`: finds captioned images, starts the interactive review, writes edits, records verdicts, saves the report. Never raises except on cancel; failures become a "skipped" report with a reason. |
| `captions.py` | The only code that writes into the dataset: `collect_verifiable_images` (skips `plk_bbox__` region crops), `apply_caption_edits` (atomic write, stays inside the dataset, backs up the original once). |
| `generation.py` | `make_caption_generator`: the function the UI calls to render one preview PNG (seed handling, file naming, pruning old re-rolls). |
| `t2i.py` | `T2IRuntime`: loads the text-to-image pipeline once, guards it with a lock (UI calls come from another thread), renders, reports token truncation, supports cancel mid-render. |
| `catalog.py` | The list of offered models (SDXL, FLUX.2 klein, Krea 2, SD 1.5, ...), old-id aliases, dropdown choices and `auto` pick by GPU memory. |
| `plan.py` | `resolve_plan`: turns config + GPU memory into a `GenerationPlan` (quantization, CPU offload, size). Pure logic, no torch. |
| `loader.py` | Builds the diffusers pipeline for a plan (pipeline class, single-file or repo id, quantization, offload, VAE tiling). Also `preview_dir_for`. |
| `weights.py` | Measures how many bytes of model weights have loaded, for a real progress bar. |
| `load_status.py` | Watches the load (tqdm bars + weight bytes) and sends periodic progress text to the UI. |
| `runtime_env.py` | Small best-effort torch helpers: GPU probe, CPU random generator, freeing memory. |
| `verdicts.py` | Opens each item on its last verdict and saves this run's verdicts to the ledger. |
| `reports.py` | One report shape for success, partial and skipped runs (a test enforces equal keys). |

## How it works
- Input: the working dataset (images that already have a `.txt`), a `CaptionVerifierConfig`, and an interaction provider.
- Without an interactive provider (normal CLI run) the step only writes a "skipped" report; it is a UI-only review.
- The model loads lazily on the first preview. You re-roll previews, judge each caption, and may edit the text.
- **apply_caption_edits**: edited text is written exactly as typed (no concept token re-added, on purpose).
- Verdicts go to `caption_verdicts.json` beside the report; `generic`/`wrong` images become "pending" for CaptionBboxStep.
- On disk: previews in `CaptionVerifierStep_previews/` beside the step report (deleted unless `keep_previews`), original captions backed up in its `captions_before/` subfolder (always kept).

## Who uses it
- `prepare_lora_kit/invoke/caption_verifier_step.py` — pipeline adapter; `invoke/mock_caption_verifier.py` reuses `captions`, `reports`, `verdicts` for `--mock`.
- `prepare_lora_kit/pipeline/configs/caption_verifier_config.py`, `project/config_schema/steps/caption_verifier.py`, `settings/payload.py` — use `catalog` for validation and dropdowns.
- `prepare_lora_kit_ui/runner/caption_verify_interaction.py` and `static/steps/caption_verify/` — the review UI.
- Tests: `tests/steps/caption_verifier/`, `tests/ui/dev/caption_verify/`, `tests/pipeline/test_caption_verdict_loop.py`

## Good to know
- `t2i.unload()` (module-level "drop every cached pipeline") is only called from tests; the step uses `T2IRuntime.unload()`.
